title: Crime & Punishment: Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the four classic aims of punishment and the main causes of crime.
meta_desc: GCSE RS Crime & Punishment foundations — aims of punishment and causes of crime.
final_note: You now know the four aims of punishment and the main causes of crime.

concepts.def: Punishment as deserved payback for wrongdoing
Punishment to change the offender for the better
Punishment to keep society safe from offenders
An action that breaks the law of the land
An action that breaks the law of God

walkthroughs.body_html:
The four classic aims are retribution, deterrence, reformation and protection.

Retribution: 'an eye for an eye' (Exodus 21:24) — proportional payback.

Deterrence: discourage the offender and others.

Reformation: rehabilitate so they don't reoffend. Protection: keep the public safe.

Key causes studied at GCSE include: poverty, upbringing, mental illness, addiction, greed, peer pressure, and opposition to unjust law (e.g. civil rights activists).

Christianity teaches we have free will but live in a fallen world. Islam teaches Allah will judge intentions on the Last Day.

A crime breaks the law of the land; a sin breaks God's law. They often overlap (e.g. murder) but not always — lying is usually a sin but not always a crime.

Some acts (e.g. apartheid laws) were legal but sinful; some acts (e.g. helping refugees illegally) may be legal crimes but moral duties.
